Definition: from G1909 and G4098; to embrace (with affection) or seize (with more or less violence; literally or figuratively):--fall into (on, upon) lie on, press upon.
BiblicalUsage: Epipipto means to fall upon — to embrace, to seize, to come over. The father ran and fell on the prodigal's neck and kissed him; the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word at Cornelius's house; fear fell on all at Ephesus; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee fell on me.
TheologicalSignificance: A father's embrace, the Spirit's coming, and Christ bearing reproaches that were not His own — that is what falls upon us. I hold that what falls reveals the heart of God, and the prodigal's welcome is the picture I should carry into every return.
